info.description: Backend API for ATLAS regulated AI/ML model development.

post.description:
Upload a CSV file and store it as the RAW dataset in DATASTORE.

NOTE: Your current Step01_DataAcquisition.tsx uses /api/data/set_sample
with JSON rows. This endpoint is kept for compatibility / future use.

schema.title: Response Upload Csv Api Data Upload Csv Post

post.description:
Legacy-compatible endpoint used by Step01_DataAcquisition.tsx.

Payload shape:

    {
      "project_id": "...",
      "headers": [...],
      "rows": [ {col: val, ...}, ... ],
      "target": "TARGET" | null,
      "selected_columns": [...]
    }

We:
  • Build a DataFrame from rows
  • Store it into DATASTORE.raw_df, scoped to (user, project_id)
  • Optionally set DATASTORE.target

get.description:
Front-end (Step06_Train.tsx) calls this to determine:

  • Which algorithms are available (`availability`)
  • Human-readable model labels (`labels`)

Expected response shape on the frontend:

  {
    ok: boolean,
    availability: { [key: string]: boolean },
    labels: { [key: string]: string }
  }

The reported availability is environment-wide (which ML libraries are
installed), not project-specific data -- but TRAINER.get_availability()
writes its result into RESULTS.model_availability internally (see
trainer_service.py), so this still requires project_id/authorization
like every other endpoint that touches RESULTS (Stage 3).

schema.title: Response Get Model Availability Api Models Availability Get

post.description:
Core training endpoint used by the Step06 Training page.

Request body (from Step06_Train.tsx):

  {
    models: string[],        // e.g. ["logreg", "xgb"]
    k_folds: number,         // 2–5, chosen in the UI
    max_parallel: number,    // future use
    calibrate: boolean,      // future use
    use_pca: boolean,        // future use
    grid_search: boolean,    // optional hyperparameter search
    grid_search_level: string // quick | balanced | thorough
  }

Response shape consumed by the frontend:

  {
    ok: boolean,
    summary: {
      ranked: [
        { key, name, auc, pr_auc, accuracy, f1 },
        ...
      ],
      n_train: number,
      n_test: number,
      k_folds: number,
      status: string
    },
    rows: number,    // convenience echo (n_train)
    status: string   // mirrors summary.status
  }

get.description:
Used by:
  • Step06_Train.tsx (to render the summary table after training)
  • Step08_Evaluation.tsx (leaderboard + default model selection)

Returns whatever the last successful /model/train call stored in RESULTStore.

project_id is now required and authorized (Stage 3): RESULTS is scoped
by (user_id, project_id), so a caller can only ever read their own
project's own last summary in the first place. The dataset_version/
target/problem_type soft-mismatch check below remains meaningful (it
detects a stale summary from an earlier feature/split configuration
within the SAME project); the project_id entry in that same check is now
redundant with the scope isolation itself but is left in place as a
harmless, defense-in-depth no-op -- it can never trigger under correct
scope resolution, since `last` (if present) can only ever be this
project's own summary.

post.description:
Creates a governed Target Intelligence evidence artifact.

Every governance fact is resolved here, in this order, before anything is
written:

  1. project authorization
  2. dataset authorization (`require_dataset`)
  3. the dataset is actually linked to this project
  4. the registered version and its immutable artifact resolve
  5. the target exists in THAT version
  6. the analysis is recomputed server-side (cached, so this is a cache read)
  7. the resolved scope is governed

A workspace draft analysis therefore cannot become governed evidence, no
matter what the request claims -- there is no request field that can assert
it, and the figures written are the server's, not the client's.

AnalyticalQueryRequest.title: AnalyticalQueryRequest
AnalyticalQueryRequest.description: Client-supplied query. `userId` is deliberately absent -- see module docstring.

TargetEvidenceRequest.title: TargetEvidenceRequest
TargetEvidenceRequest.description:
Only ANALYTICAL SELECTION comes from the client.

Deliberately absent: scope mode, evidence eligibility, class counts, event
rate, imbalance, interval, checksum, population rows. Every one of those is
derived on the server, so a crafted request cannot assert governance or
substitute figures. Fields a client sends that are not on this model are
rejected by pydantic rather than carried through.

TargetProfileRequest.title: TargetProfileRequest
TargetProfileRequest.description:
Only SELECTION comes from the client.

Deliberately absent: scope mode, profile scope, exact status, evidence
eligibility, artifact checksum, population size, governance status. Extra
fields are rejected rather than carried, so a crafted request cannot assert
that a preview is a governed population.

server__eda__workspace_types__TargetByPr.title: TargetByPredictorRequest
server__eda__workspace_types__TargetByPr.description:
On-demand Target-by-Predictor over the full in-memory backend population.

Used when the project has no registered Dataset Library version, so the
DuckDB-over-artifact path in
server/analytics/target_intelligence_service.py has no immutable
(dataset, version) to scan. The result shape is identical, and the summary
is produced by the same shared function, so the two paths cannot disagree.
